newsitem.title: CHINA: China-German JV breaks ground on car design centre.
newsitem.headline: China-German JV breaks ground on car design centre.

text.p: China-German joint venture Shanghai Volkswagen Automotive Co Ltd on Friday broke ground on a $120 million-research and development centre that will be used to design cars in China, Volkswagen executives said.
The joint venture partners -- Germany's Volkswagen AG and China's state-owned Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp (Group) -- will fund the centre, which will be completed by 1999, they said.

"China has built up the plants and facilities for producing cars in high volume," Kurt Rippholz, a spokesman for Volkswagen AG said after the ground breaking ceremony. "Now China has to take the next step to design its own cars."
Volkswagen AG chief executive officer Ferdinand Piech, who is on a four-day visit to China, told reporters the German side will provide its latest technology to the centre.
But Piech said he was not sure when a car designed at the centre would roll off the assembly line.

Shanghai Volkswagen, which was set up in 1985, on Friday produced its 800,000th Santana car, executives said. The joint venture produced 200,222 cars in 1996 and aims to boost production to 250,000 in 1997, they said.
Shanghai Volkswagen had over 52 percent of the domestic car market in 1996 with sales of 24.31 billion yuan, according to the company.

Piech will on Saturday visit VW's other China joint venture, located in the northeast city of Changchun, to mark the production of its 100,000th Audi car and the start of production of a more powerful engine to be used in its Jetta cars, executives said.
The joint venture was set up in 1991 with China's First Auto Works.
Piech earlier this week met with Chinese President Jiang Zemin in Beijing for discussions, executives said, but declined to give further details.
